title: fix(types): type ObjectGallerySchema.filter as its documented destination
body:
Fixes #9309

`ObjectGallerySchema.filter` is typed as the destination its own docblock names, on both faces. Drafted by an ObjectUI development agent seat (Claude Code) in session `session_01L5xpA5q533BgTTNADibEFt`; every figure below was re-derived on this branch and each one carries the command that produced it.

## The defect — the half of the card that holds

`packages/types/src/objectql.ts`, in `ObjectGallerySchema`:

```ts
/** Query filter, forwarded verbatim as `$filter` */
filter?: unknown;
```

`$filter` is `QueryParams['$filter']` in `packages/types/src/data.ts` — `Record<string, any> | FilterArray`. So the declaration named a destination it did not type: an author told to forward the value verbatim got a type error on the key the sentence had just told them to forward, and the way through was `as`, which un-checks the destination's real type at that call site too. AGENTS.md #0.1 points the other way — repair the declaration, do not widen the consumer.

The member is now an **indexed access** on `QueryParams`, not a copy of its arms, so the declaration cannot drift away from the slot the docblock names.

## What does NOT hold — my own census, counting rule beside the number

The card calls this "the one view schema of six that is not `any[]`". Re-derived on this branch, that framing does not survive.

**Counting rule:** every optional `filter` property signature in `packages/types/src/objectql.ts`, charged to its owning interface by the **TypeScript parser** (nearest enclosing `interface` declaration in the AST) — never by proximity to the nearest preceding `export interface` line. Line numbers are deliberately absent: two landings moved this file by +241 lines the day the card was taken.

| owning interface | spelling (before this PR) |
|---|---|
| `ObjectGridSchema` | `any[]` |
| **`NamedListView`** | `any[]` |
| `ObjectMapSchema` | `any[]` |
| `ObjectGanttSchema` | `any[]` |
| `ObjectCalendarSchema` | `any[]` |
| `ObjectKanbanSchema` | `any[]` |
| **`ObjectChartSchema`** | **`any[] \| Record<string, any>`** |
| `ObjectGallerySchema` | **`unknown`** — this card |
| **`ObjectDataTableSchema`** | **`any`** |

**Nine declarations, four spellings.** Two independent instruments agree: a comment-blanking brace walk and a TypeScript AST walk, both run on this branch, and both refuse the proximity answer on a fixture where the two rules differ. So one of the "six siblings" is `NamedListView`, which is not a view schema at all, and the population is nine rather than seven.

That kills a **justification**, not the finding. It specifically kills the card's first repair option *as argued* — "`any[]` (match the six siblings, one vocabulary)" — because there is no one vocabulary to match.

## The disposition, and the ground it was chosen on

**Chosen: `filter?: QueryParams['$filter']`, on the destination-typing ground** — the type the docblock itself names, reached by indexed access so the two cannot drift. ⛔ Not on "the siblings all say `any[]`", which is false.

Two grounds were rejected, and both for measured reasons:

- **`any[]` (array-only).** `QueryParams['$filter']` accepts the ObjectQL field-keyed record too, and `data.ts`'s own docblock names both forms as normal. Declaring only the array arm would refuse the record form that the destination accepts — over-narrowing against the sentence being honoured.
- **Leaving the zod mirror at `z.unknown()`.** Measured, not assumed: with the TS face narrowed and the mirror reverted, `zod-mirror-parity` stays green at **32/32** and `tsc -p tsconfig.test.json` exits 0, because that file's `Unconstrained` predicate excludes an `unknown` mirror slot from its wider-than-declared comparison **by definition**. The split would have been real and unreported. Both faces move together for that reason.

The census this PR removes from prose is re-derived instead by `packages/types/src/__tests__/object-gallery-filter-9309.test.ts`, which walks the AST on every run (AGENTS.md #9 — point at the instrument, never write down its answer).

## Accept-set change, stated plainly

NARROWS, both faces. `unknown` is the widest type there is, so every value the new declaration refuses used to compile: `filter: 'stage=won'` and `filter: 42` are type errors now, and the mirror refuses them at parse time. Both object arms are unchanged and no runtime behaviour moves — the value still travels to `$filter` byte-for-byte.

## The consumer count, measured

The card asserts nothing in this repository could read the key without asserting it first. Measured on this branch:

- `ObjectGallerySchema` is imported by exactly one non-test source outside `@object-ui/types`: `packages/plugin-list/src/ObjectGallery.tsx`. `ObjectQLComponentSchema`, the union arm through which the type could otherwise be reached, is imported by `packages/cli` and by tests only.
- Three sites build `{ type: 'object-gallery', ... }` nodes — `plugin-list/src/ListView.tsx`, `plugin-view/src/ObjectView.tsx`, `plugin-detail/src/RelatedList.tsx`. None of the three literals is annotated with this interface.
  - ⚠️ **CORRECTION, written in by the `domain:ui#2` execution seat.** The sentence that stood here also said 「None of them sets `filter` on the gallery node」, and that half is **FALSE**. It was falsified by the at-tier contract review on this PR and then re-derived by this seat on `origin/main`: `plugin-list/src/ListView.tsx` builds `const baseProps = {` carrying `filter: schema.filter,`, and spreads `...baseProps` into the `type: 'object-gallery'` literal — so that node DOES carry `filter`.
  - ⭐ The zero-breakage conclusion survives, on grounds measured rather than assumed: that file never names `ObjectGallerySchema` at all (**0** occurrences; control, same command, `ListViewSchema` **22**), so the literal is never checked against this member — and `ListViewSchema.filter` is `z.array(z.any())`, which is assignable to the new type either way. ⇒ the claim was wrong and the conclusion it supported is right for a different reason, which is exactly why it is corrected here rather than left to be discovered as a contradiction later.
- `@object-ui/plugin-list` type-checks clean against the rebuilt declaration (exit 0), and `@object-ui/cli` likewise.

⚠️ That in-repo zero is not a claim about downstream consumers. The change is breaking for any TypeScript consumer that assigned a non-object value to this key.

## Evidence

**Reverse validation, both legs mutated on disk and restored byte-identically (`git hash-object` compared before and after; trap-restored):**

- Reverting the TS member to `unknown` turns **four** independent things red: the census test (2 assertions), the `Equal` pin and its `unknown` control (TS2344 twice), both `@ts-expect-error` directives (TS2578 twice), **and** `zod-mirror-parity.test.ts` itself (TS2322 at the gallery pair) — the ledger sees the mismatch once the mirror is narrowed, which it could not before.
- Reverting the zod mirror to `z.unknown()` turns the runtime refusal red on `filter: 'stage=won'` while the parity suite stays green — the blind-spot measurement quoted above.
- A cross-package leg: a temporary literal assigning a string to this key inside `plugin-list` makes that package's type-check red with `TS2322 ... not assignable to type 'Record<string, any> | FilterArray | undefined'`, which is what proves the green above was read off the **rebuilt** `.d.ts` and not a cache. Probe removed; file restored byte-identically.

**Runs (all foreground, heavy ones serialised through the shared verify lock):**

| run | result |
|---|---|
| `pnpm exec vitest run packages/types/ packages/plugin-list/` | 269 files / 5346 tests passed |
| `pnpm --filter @object-ui/types run type-check` | exit 0 |
| `pnpm --filter @object-ui/plugin-list run type-check` | exit 0 (after building its dependency closure) |
| `pnpm --filter @object-ui/cli run type-check` | exit 0 |
| `pnpm --filter @object-ui/types build` | exit 0; narrowing verified present in `dist/objectql.d.ts` |
| `node scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs` | exit 0 — 1 changeset declared |
| `pnpm run check:control-bytes` | exit 0 |
| `node scripts/check-governed-queue-guard.mjs --test` | NOT GOVERNED — 4 paths, none matched |

Baseline before any edit, same command, same tree: `packages/types/` 190 files / 4372 tests passed.

## Acceptance notes

Residuals named, ⛔ none of them done here. This card's scope is `ObjectGallerySchema.filter` and nothing else.

1. **`ObjectDataTableSchema.filter` is `any`** — the widest of the nine spellings, and the one that defeats the checker outright rather than merely under-describing. Worth its own card.
2. **`ObjectChartSchema.filter` is `any[] | Record<string, any>`** — a hand-spelled near-copy of the same destination, and its own docblock says narrowing to the spec's array-only `FilterArray` is now a deprecation rather than a defect (objectui#8944 removed the blocker). Worth its own card.
3. **`NamedListView.filter` is counted as a sibling view schema in at least three places** — the card, `ObjectChartSchema`'s docblock (repaired here, see below) and `packages/plugin-dashboard/src/ObjectPivotTable.tsx`. It is the named-view interface, not a view schema. Category error.
4. **`ObjectPivotTable.tsx` names an interface that declares no `filter` at all.** Its comment lists `ObjectViewSchema` among six array-only owners; measured, `ObjectViewSchema` declares none, and the sixth owner is `NamedListView`. So that comment is wrong in both directions at once. Untouched — outside this PR's declared file surface.
5. **`packages/plugin-list/src/ObjectGallery.tsx` still carries `schema.filter as QueryParams['$filter']`** plus a comment describing the key as "declared `unknown` — the one view schema in `@object-ui/types` whose `filter` is not `any[]`". After this PR the assertion is a redundant identity cast and the comment is false. ⚠️ **Falsified by this change, and NOT repaired here**: `plugin-list` is outside the file surface this round declared, and the declared handling for a breach is to stop and report it rather than widen the PR. It wants a follow-up.
6. **`packages/types/src/zod/objectql.zod.ts`'s `ObjectChartSchema` comment** still says narrowing is "blocked on the drill-down spread", which its TS twin says objectui#8944 already repaired. Pre-existing, untouched.
7. **`.changeset/objectchart-schema-anchor-7946.md`** carries the same "six sibling `object-*` widgets ... are already array-only" sentence. It is a release note for work already done; not edited.

**One in-file repair beyond the gallery key, declared rather than smuggled.** `ObjectChartSchema`'s docblock called that key "the only `object-*` `filter` with a record arm". This PR's own change makes that false — the gallery now has a record arm — so the sentence is repaired in the same commit, in the same file, and it now points at the census test instead of carrying a count. Nothing about `ObjectChartSchema`'s **type** moves.
